themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests have surged 700% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks, z-score: 5.42), suggesting either a sudden infrastructure failure, removal of baskets, or acute sanitation problem in high-traffic Midtown areas.
evidence: 3 litter basket complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
700% spike with z-score of 5.42 (statistically significant anomaly)
Timing coincides with potential street maintenance cycle or budget constraint
reporting_angles: Did Sanitation or Parks remove baskets from specific Midtown blocks this week? Why?
Interview street-level workers and residents in Herald Square, Times Square areas about visibility and cleanliness shifts

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal complaints jumped 146% LAST WEEK (49 complaints vs. 19.9 weekly average, z-score: 4.15), a sharp spike that suggests either systematic failures in signal infrastructure or a pattern of malfunctioning signals at key Midtown intersections affecting commuter safety and flow.
evidence: 49 traffic signal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 19.9 weekly average (8-week baseline)
146% increase with z-score of 4.15 (strong statistical signal)
Localized to Midtown grid with heavy pedestrian/vehicle traffic
reporting_angles: Map which intersections (5th Ave, Broadway, 42nd St area?) are affected most and if there's a pattern
Contact DOT to determine if signal system maintenance, power issues, or equipment failures are responsible

themes_detail.label: Water Infrastructure Problems
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints peaked at 45 THREE WEEKS AGO (224% above 8-week average of 13.9, z-score: 4.83), indicating possible main breaks, pressure issues, or building-level water failures affecting multiple properties across the district.
evidence: 45 water system complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 13.9 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Timing suggests event-driven issue rather than chronic baseline problem
reporting_angles: Did DEP respond to a water main break or pressure drop in Midtown 3 weeks ago? Map affected buildings.
Follow up: Has the spike resolved or are complaints still elevated this week compared to prior baseline?

themes_detail.label: Rodent & Pest Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked 380% THREE WEEKS AGO (6 complaints vs. 1.2 weekly average, z-score: 3.66), aligning with long-standing community board budget requests for rat control—a renewed signal that pest management is failing in Midtown's dense commercial/residential mix.
evidence: 6 rodent complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Aligns with recurring CB budget request for animal/pest control funding (repeated year-over-year)
reporting_angles: Did a construction project, restaurant opening, or waste management disruption trigger the spike 3 weeks ago?
Interview DOHMH about current rodent abatement strategy in Midtown; why does CB keep requesting more funding if baseline is low?

themes_detail.label: Building Safety Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints surged 380% TWO WEEKS AGO (3 complaints vs. 0.6 weekly average, z-score: 3.41), suggesting isolated but serious building condition or occupancy safety incidents that warrant investigation given Midtown's dense floor-plate commercial stock.
evidence: 3 safety complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
311 category too broad; needs drill-down into specific building or incident type
reporting_angles: Request detailed 311 data: which buildings, what type of safety issues (fire hazard, structural, occupancy)?
Cross-reference with DOB permit filings (3832 filed in last 90 days, mostly alterations) to identify if renovations triggered violations
